# Lumail.io

> The AI-native email platform for newsletters, automations, and transactional email.

Lumail lets teams and AI agents create campaigns, manage subscribers, automate email workflows, send transactional messages, and inspect delivery analytics from one organization-scoped platform. The browser application includes a visual email editor, capture pages, sending-domain setup, campaign scheduling, workflow automation, and deliverability controls. The same product surface is available to software and agents through OAuth, a hosted Model Context Protocol server, a REST API, a TypeScript SDK, and the Lumail CLI.

## Agent access

- MCP server: Streamable HTTP endpoint protected by OAuth 2.1 or organization API tokens.
- MCP server manifest: machine-readable transport, OAuth, documentation, and OpenAPI discovery.
- MCP install guide: machine-readable client setup instructions.
- OpenAPI 3.1 specification: typed REST operations and JSON error schemas.
- Agent documentation index: concise markdown index of every agent and developer resource.
- Full markdown documentation: concatenated public documentation for offline retrieval.

## Developer access

- REST API reference: subscriber, tag, event, campaign, and transactional-email operations.
- Authentication: organization-scoped bearer tokens and permissions.
- TypeScript SDK: typed application integration.
- CLI: install and operate Lumail from a terminal.
- MCP reference: transports, authentication, tools, resources, and limits.

## Product and support

- Pricing
- Documentation
- Support
- Sitemap

Lumail.io is operated by Codelynx, LLC, 8 The Green STE B, Dover Delaware 19901, United States. Contact contact@lumail.io for product or developer support.

Pricing | Lumail.io

# You pay for emails sent. Never for subscribers stored.

Type how many emails you send a month. We pick the cheapest plan and the bill for that volume.

Emails you send each month

Type a number or drag the slider.

Free

For a list that pays for itself.

Business

High volume, more seats, lower rate per email.

Transactional and marketing email share the same quota. No card for the free plan.

## Questions about pricing

Do you charge per subscriber?+

No. There is no subscriber limit on any plan, and no line on your invoice for list size. Import 50,000 contacts on day one if you want. The price only moves when you send.

So what will it actually cost me?+

The first 3,000 emails each month are free, no card required. Creator is $20/month with 40,000 emails included. A 20,000-contact list emailed four times a month is 80,000 emails, costing $48. Use the calculator for your volume.

How is this different from Mailchimp, Kit, or Beehiiv?+

Some competitors now expose MCP too, so compare the real workflow instead of the AI label. Lumail's full catalog has 126 organization-scoped tools across campaigns, workflows, subscribers, analytics, and transactional email, with a visual app, CLI, SDK, and API beside them. The billing model is the other difference: Lumail prices emails delivered and stores unlimited subscribers, so a dormant record does not raise your bill.

Can Lumail send my app's transactional emails too?+

Yes, and that's the point. Point your app at our SMTP relay (smtp.lumail.io:587, STARTTLS) or the API and your password resets, receipts, and OTPs ship from the same place as your newsletter. They travel in a separate instant lane, so a 50,000-recipient campaign can never make a login code wait.

Do I need to be a developer to use Lumail?+

No. Everything runs from the dashboard: a visual workflow builder, a filter builder for segments, and an AI-assisted editor. The API and SDK are there when you want them, not a prerequisite.

Can my AI agent run my newsletter?+

If you already work in Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP client, add your API token and 126 organization-aware tools show up. Ask for a campaign, a segment, or last month's numbers and the agent does it. Entirely optional. The dashboard does the same job.

content.text:
`video.mp4` (45 s, 1920×1080, 16:9) and `index.html` (the player) are both in the working directory. I checked the MP4 with ffprobe and played it in Chrome through the HTML player.

**What the video shows**

I took the brand look from lumail.io: the red-orange gradient logo tile with the white "L", warm off-white and near-black backgrounds, and Geist type. The copy and numbers come from the site (126 tools, 3,000 free emails, $20 for 40,000 emails, the Mailchimp migration demo). Scenes are separated by red or dark wipes.

| Time | Scene |
|---|---|
| 0–4.5 s | Hook: "Running email marketing shouldn't feel like a second job." Pain-point chips (Templates, Tuesday night, Looks like 2019) get sucked away. |
| 4.5–9 s | Logo reveal on the red gradient, with the tagline "The AI tools that will make you love email marketing." |
| 9–17 s | Agents/MCP: a typed terminal query, three tool calls returning 312 each, and a counter reaching 126 tools. |
| 17–24 s | Editor: subject and body typing, the `{{first_name}}` variable, an AI "Tighten" rewrite, and an inbox preview. |
| 24–30 s | Workflow builder: nodes and connectors draw in, with an A/B badge and a yes/no branch. |
| 30–35.5 s | Migration: competitor chips fly into the logo, then 12,847 contacts, 14 tags and 3 workflows count up to "Ready in 8 minutes." |
| 35.5–40.5 s | Pricing: "Pay for emails sent. Never for subscribers stored." with ∞, 3,000 and $20 cards. |
| 40.5–45 s | CTA: "Import your list. Send tonight." with a "Start free" button and lumail.io. |

I couldn't view the frames directly, only text descriptions of them. That was enough to confirm the layout and copy, but not pixel-level polish.

**Checks**
- **MP4:** H.264, 1920×1080, square pixels, 30 fps, duration 45.000 s.
- **Player:** I tested four viewport sizes, from 2000×600 to 700×1200. The video always fits with the full frame visible, no cropping or distortion, and it plays with native controls and no visible heading.
- **Title:** the browser tab title is "Claude Sonnet 5.5".
- **Autoplay:** the player autoplays muted, because browsers block unmuted autoplay.

The video has no audio track, since you didn't ask for one.

I used pnpm only. To re-render, run `pnpm render`. It uses `scene.html` and `render.mjs`, which draw each frame in Chrome and encode with ffmpeg.
